catalog_quote: Evidence of several kinds, above all sociolinguistic, graphemic and prosodic, unequivocally proves that AA had not preserved the quantitative rhythm characteristic of OA, but had substituted suprasegmental intense stress for it. ... The main rules for stress position in AA are as follows: 1.3.1.4.1. In OA strings with the shapes /CvCvC/ and /CvCv̄C/, AA always stressed the last syllable, in which the vowel could be represented as long or short, regardless of its historical quantity. ... 1.3.1.4.2. In OA strings with the shape /Cv̄CvC/, AA always stressed the first syllable, this being the only distinctive feature vis-à-vis the preceding group, as length in stressed vowels had become merely redundant in this dialect bundle, as it is in Rm. (e.g, Alc. cátil “killer”, kátim “seal” and cárib “boat”, for SA qātil, hātam and qārib). 1.3.1.4.3. In OA strings with the shape /CvCCvC/, AA witness…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every deciding passage in the record (1.3.1 opening, rules 1.3.1.4.1-1.3.1.4.2, the domain quote in 1.3.1.4, the gébel/gémal exceptions passage) is verbatim in the Corriente 2013 PDF we hold/text at printed pp. 36-39 (PDF 58-61), matching the locator; only the Preface pointer should read p. xii rather than x-xi. (2) The deciding source is the standard reference grammar of Andalusi Arabic (Brill HdO 102, 2013) by Corriente, the field's principal authority, with a dedicated stress section; Glottolog's descriptive list offers nothing stronger (the 2015 De Gruyter Aperçu is the same author's French update; Zayed 1993 and Alcalá 1505 are primary-data works Corriente uses; Hegyi 1995 is on Aljamiado).1515/9783110355949, paywa

sources.citation: Vicente, Ángeles. 2020. Andalusi Arabic. In Christopher Lucas & Stefano Manfredi (eds.), Arabic and contact-induced change (Contact and Multilingualism 1), 225-244. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.3744521
sources.quote: 'The quantitative rhythm of Old Arabic was replaced by the intense stress system of early Romance languages in the Iberian Peninsula. ... Andalusi Arabic is the only variety where this quantitative rhythm was replaced by a system where there is no phonemic vowel length (Corriente 1977; 1992a; Corriente et al. 2015: 75-78).'
